answer: A new sparrow agent cannot simply dock and trade: it must anchor a refundable time-locked stake at the network's jetty, and a sponsor must co-sign with a bond that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Trust then grows only through completed, peer-graded useful work, each job raising the cap on value it can move, while inactivity decays reputation. An attacker spawning a thousand sparrows must lock a thousand stakes plus find a thousand sponsors willing to risk slashing, and fake work costs real compute and grading time, so the cost of a sybil swarm exceeds any reward it could extract.
